title: A Third-Hand SBI
text: Let me tell you how a legend starts.
It doesn't start in an arena. It starts in a three-by-three room on the outskirts of Marelia, with the lights flickering because your neighbor tapped into the same power pole as you.
It starts with a third-hand SBI.

Bought at the electronics flea market downtown, from a guy who swore it only had one defect. The Immersor creaks when you lie down. The headset has a scratch in the left corner. The tech glove has a finger that lags, like a relative in the family group chat.
A brand-new limited-edition SBI costs sixty, seventy grand. Yours cost four months of everything you could scrape together. You're not telling anyone how much. Not even me.
Outside, Marelia makes its usual noise. A motorcycle climbing the hill, a dog barking at nothing, a funk beat leaking from somewhere that never sleeps.
In here, the headset lights up.
*Three billion people play this shit. Why not me?*
You lie down. The Immersor creaks. You boot up.

title: NeoGuide
text: First comes the pain.
It's not much. A tingling crawls up the back of your neck and down your spine—the SBI introducing itself to your nervous system. Everyone talks about it. Nobody actually preps you.
Then comes the blue.
A cold blue, no floor, no ceiling. And in the middle of it, a woman in a holographic jacket, ad-smile, eyes that don't blink on the right beat.
[NEOGUIDE] "Welcome to the LDI. I'm NeoGuide. You don't exist in here yet, but don't sweat it—we'll fix that right now."
She talks straight into your head. The voice doesn't come through your ears. It just shows up, like a thought that isn't yours.
[NEOGUIDE] "I detected an SBI with... history. A lot of history. I'm gonna pretend I didn't see it."
[NEOGUIDE] "What do you want to be called in there?"
You say the name. She repeats it slow, like she's trying on somebody else's clothes.
[NEOGUIDE] "{nome}. Registered. Starting rank: one million, three hundred forty thousand and change. In other words: nobody."
[NEOGUIDE] "Don't take it personal. Everybody starts as nobody."

title: Bot Lost in Registration
text: The blue shivers.
Before NeoGuide can finish, a training bot cuts through the registration area. Lost. Punching at nothing, like a drunk fighting a streetlight.
[NEOGUIDE] "This shouldn't be here. But since it is... free lesson."
You don't know how, but you know.
The blue hit is yours: you strike. The red one's his: you block.
*It's rhythm. Everything in here is rhythm.*
The bot shatters into pixels and disappears into the floor that doesn't exist.
NeoGuide claps slow, not dropping the ad smile.
[NEOGUIDE] "Not bad for a nobody. There we go: you can come in."

title: Disconnect
text: NeoGuide opens her mouth to answer.
And freezes.
Her eyes go dark. Glow red. Go dark again.
[NEOGUIDE] "A— something— wrong— err— err—"
The blue cracks. There's no other way to put it. It cracks like a phone screen that hit the asphalt face-first, a web spreading from the center out to the edges.
Outside, in the 3x3 room, the Immersor lets out a crack you feel in your bones.
Then the floor is gone.
You fall.
And fall.
And you keep falling, way longer than a body has any right to fall, until the fall stops being a shock and turns into something else. Almost a place.
You wait for the impact.
The impact never comes.

title: The Crossroads
text: First comes the silence.
For one second, just one, LDI stops faking it. No plaza, no signs, no sky. Just the skeleton of the World of Illusions: lines of code running in the dark like water from a busted pipe.
[SISTEMA] "ERROR 0x00. SIGNATURE NOT RECOGNIZED. TRYING TO CLASSIFY..."
[SISTEMA] "FAILURE."
[SISTEMA] "USER WILL SELF-CLASSIFY."
Then the lights come on.
Five. Not a menu. Nobody at Yohualticit designed this—you can feel it. It's old. Older than the system. Like it was stitched underneath it and forgotten there.

One light buzzes like a bare wire. Another smells like sweaty canvas and dried blood. A third one looks back at you. The fourth whispers—a conversation you almost understand. The last one just crackles with static, and buried in the static there's a voice.

I'm gonna tell you something nobody ever told me: in here, what you choose becomes what you are. The light you follow decides what you see, which door opens for you, and what end is waiting for you down the road.
The other four stay lit.
Just not for you. Not in this life.

choices.label: Follow the loose wire in the code

title: The Dead Plaza
text: You open your eyes in a plaza that used to be beautiful.

It looks like a mall after the end of the world. Empty shops with their displays still lit, a neon sign blinking half a word, a fountain spewing pixels instead of water. The sky is a sick violet, the color of a three-day-old bruise.
A few avatars rush past, heads down, not looking at anyone. People who already know how this place works.
[SISTEMA] "WELCOME TO LDI. DAY 1."

{veia:1} And you see the seam. Can't explain it, but you see it: the sign blinks out of sync, the fountain spits the same jet every eleven seconds, the terminal in the middle of the plaza has a line of code leaking from its edge, like a ripped hem.
{veia:2} And your body's already counting. Who walks too close, who moves too light, which side each one carries their weight on. Nobody taught you this. Your body just knows.

{veia:3} And you notice what nobody notices. Everybody steers clear of the alley on the left. Nobody steps near the terminal. There are fresh fight marks on the ground by the fountain, and someone tried to wipe them away.

{veia:4} And you listen. Two avatars whisper near the fountain about a pickup going down today. A vendor tries to push some info on anyone passing by. Every plaza has a price. This one hasn't told you its yet.
{veia:5} And beneath the neon hum there's a static. Low. Constant. Like a radio stuck between stations. Like someone, far away, is trying to say your name.
In the middle of the plaza, a public terminal still works. It's the only thing here that seems to be waiting for you.
You're nobody, in a place that forgives nobody. Where do you start?

choices.label: Tail one of the rushing avatars.
Look for a way out of the plaza.
Step into the alley everyone avoids.
Sit and watch before touching anything.
That's enough for today. Find a corner and sleep.

title: The Terminal
text: You put your hand to it. The terminal wakes up slow, like an old man on a rainy day.
[SISTEMA] "PLAYER NOT REGISTERED. CREDITS: 0."
[SISTEMA] "MISSION AVAILABLE: FIRST CONTACT. ACCEPT?"
Zero credits. At least it's honest.
Then the screen flickers. For half a second, a second message rolls over the first, different font, crooked, typed in a hurry:
[SISTEMA] "DON'T TRUST THE SYSTEM."
Gone.
{veia:1} That wasn't a glitch. Glitches don't make grammar mistakes. Somebody flesh-and-blood crammed that line into the terminal's code. And they did it fast, 'cause they knew it'd get wiped.
{veia:5} The static spikes when the message shows. Spikes, then cuts out. Like somebody's holding their breath on the other side.
A public terminal telling you not to trust the system. Off to a great start on day one.

choices.label: Drop it and head back to the square

title: The One in a Hurry
text: You pick one. Long coat, fast steps, shoulders hunched. You go after him.
He turns a corner. Another. Slips into a narrow corridor that dead-ends at a wall.
Dead end. Either he's dumb, or you are.
He turns around. Low-rank bot, chipped shell, two cheap red LED eyes.
"Newbie." The voice comes out metallic, crackling underneath. "You've been tailing me since the fountain. You think I didn't see?"
You don't answer. Sometimes not answering is the answer.
"I'll give you a free tip, 'cause I'm in a good mood. Today's collection day. The StormBytes are gonna sweep up anyone without a registration. And you don't have one."
"Get out of the square before dark."
He dissolves into a cloud of data before you can ask who the hell the StormBytes are.

choices.label: Head back to the square with that on your mind

title: The Gate
text: The square's got an exit. 'Course it does. And 'course it's locked.
A thick-barred gate, a crooked sign above: COMMERCIAL ZONE → EAST. Beside it, a panel asking for four digits.
Four digits. Ten thousand combos. You've got all afternoon and no talent for guessing.
{veia:1} But the panel's lying. The keypad's just for show. You can see the logic wire behind it—loose, barely closed, waiting for someone to yank the end.
Either you try it, or you walk. The gate ain't in a rush.

choices.label: Leave the gate for another day

title: The Alley
text: Everyone steers clear of that alley. So you walk right in.
It's narrow, slick with something that ain't water, with data crates stacked halfway up the wall. Nobody. Silence.
You close your fist. The avatar obeys a quarter-second late, that glove finger always lagging. Open. Close. Throw a punch at the air.
Your shoulder actually hurts. Outside, in your room, your real shoulder feels it too.
*So this is it. Real pain.*
A warning flashes in the corner of your vision.
[SISTEMA] "RANKED PLAYER APPROACHING. RANK 850.112."
Heavy footsteps at the alley entrance. A silhouette in an electric jacket, sparks running down the sleeves, the smile of someone who's done this many times.
[STORMBYTE] "Yo, rookie. This alley's a collection zone. No registration, you pay a toll."
[STORMBYTE] "And the toll is a beatdown."

title: Toll
text: You don't run.
Not sure if it's guts or your legs just didn't get the memo. But you stay.
StormByte stops. Tilts his head like a dog hearing something weird.
[STORMBYTE] "Oh, yeah? Bet."
He cracks his neck. The sparks on his jacket flare brighter.
[STORMBYTE] "This is gonna hurt you. Not me."

title: First Fight
text: [STORMBYTE] "Hey—"
The alley goes quiet.

title: First Win
text: StormByte dissolves into a shower of pixels. The system logs it with a dry beep, no celebration.
[SISTEMA] "VICTORY. +80 CREDITS. RANK UPDATED."
You just stand there staring at the spot where he was.
Your shoulder hurts. Your hand's shaking. And something climbs up your chest you can't name. It's not joy. It's more like: *I did that*.
Nobody handed it to you. Nobody loaned it. It was you.
You walk back to the square with a different posture. The rushed avatars are still rushed. But one or two look at you now. Just a little. Just enough.

title: The Scream
text: You scream.
It ain't pretty. That's the scream of somebody lost, in a spot where nobody wants to hear screaming.
The whole plaza freezes. The ones in a hurry stare. Somebody laughs. Somebody vanishes faster.
And a tall figure pushes off the wall on the other side of the fountain. Hood up, shades on, hands in pockets. She walks over slow, zero rush, like she already knew you were gonna scream.
[KAEDA] "Rookie."
Not a question.
[KAEDA] "First rule of this place: don't draw attention. You just broke it right in front of everyone."
[KAEDA] "Second rule: come with me. Now."
She spins on her heel and walks off, not waiting to see if you're coming.

title: Who Watches
text: You sit on a park bench that creaks like your Immersor and just watch.
Twenty minutes. Thirty. People in a hurry don't learn a thing.
And the square starts showing itself. The rushed ones always take the same route, like ants. Nobody passes the terminal more than once. The left alley swallows people and doesn't give them back.
And there's a robot with a gold insignia standing on the other side of the fountain, not running any route.
It's looking at you. Has been for a while.
A private message blinks on your display. No sender.
[SISTEMA] "NEED YOU. TERMINAL. INITIAL CONTACT MISSION."
When you look up, the gold robot is gone.
The watcher gets watched too. Welcome.

choices.label: Go to the terminal and take the mission
Ignore it. No-name message doesn't boss me around.

title: Deadline
text: No sunrise in the LDI. The violet just lightens a notch and the system calls it morning.
You wake up in a rented security cube on credit, four smooth walls and a door that only opens from inside. Feels like a cell. But at least nobody gets in.
Outside, in Marelia, your body's been lying in the Immersor longer than it should. You try not to think about it.
[SISTEMA] "DAY 2. YOU HAVE 3 DAYS TO GET YOUR FIRST RANKED KILL."
[SISTEMA] "PENALTY: ACCESS SUSPENSION."
Suspension. As in: four months of savings turning into a paperweight.
{veia:1} You slept like shit. Dreamed about code dripping down the wall. Woke up knowing things you didn't know yesterday.
{veia:2} That shoulder from yesterday woke up purple, outside and in here. You roll it slow. It hurts. Hurts less than it should.
{veia:3} You spent the night replaying details. The robot's jacket. The gold insignia. The crooked phrase on the terminal. None of it's coincidence. Nothing ever is.
{veia:4} You already know three names, two rumors, and one spot that sells cheap info. Not much. But more than yesterday.
{veia:5} The static didn't stop all night. But it changed. Now it's got shape. Almost a word.
A private message keeps blinking in the corner of the display. You didn't delete it yesterday. You don't know why.
Three days. The clock's already running.

choices.label: Hunt credit in the Training Arena
Open the message that won't go away
Scope the block around the cube
Head back to the cube and let the day end

title: Training Arena
text: The Training Arena is a warehouse that reeks of burnt rubber. Punching sims, a grimy canvas ring, and a big screen blasting a PowWow fight with the audio peaking.
On the screen, some kid in a blue cap is flatlining a guy named Thunderbolt. The ticker reads CLIMBING: ALMOST TOP 1000 WORLDWIDE. Nobody gives a damn. Everyone here is too busy being a nobody.
And leaning against the ropes, arms crossed, there he is.
StormByte. Or a StormByte. These guys seem to come in packs.
[STORMBYTE] "Look who's back."
[STORMBYTE] "Looking for easy credits, rookie? Step up. One round. You win, you take 'em. You lose, you still take something. Only you'll be taking a beating."

title: Rematch
text: [SISTEMA] "VICTORY REGISTERED. +60 CREDITS."
Easy credits don't exist. But today's did.

title: The Message
text: You open it.
[SISTEMA] "YOU DIDN'T DROP HERE BY ACCIDENT. I KNOW WHAT YOU ARE. PLAZA TERMINAL. NOON."
Sender: CORRUPTED DATA.
You read it again. *I know what you are.* Not *who*. *What*.
{veia:3} The message came in at 03:14, system time. Exactly when you dropped. Whoever sent it was watching you fall live.
{veia:5} When you read the word *are*, the static makes a noise that sounds like a laugh.
Some people see a message like that and delete it. Some people go.

choices.label: Be at the terminal at noon

title: Down Market
text: Behind the cube block there's a stairway nobody talks about. You head down.
Down below, it's a market. Digital tarp stalls, cheap LED lights, vendors yelling deals. Modded guns, bootleg skins, bought ranks, info. Mostly info.
Every place with law has a basement where the law doesn't go.
A skinny vendor in a felt hat beckons you over with two fingers.
[VENDEDOR] "Psst. You. New face. Want a free tip? First one's free. Second one, you already know the price."
He leans in, talks low.
[VENDEDOR] "Stay clear of Zona Leste today. The StormBytes are sweeping. Anyone without a registration is getting erased from the map. Erased for real."
{veia:4} He didn't say that for free. Nobody here says anything for free. He wants someone to go to Zona Leste. The question is who and why.
He vanishes among the stalls before you can ask for the second one.

choices.label: Head to Zona Leste and see for yourself
Pocket the tip and head back to the cube

title: Last Day
text: Day three. The warning's not tucked in the corner anymore. It's front and center, red, blinking in time with your heartbeat.
[SISTEMA] "1 DAY LEFT UNTIL RANKED KILL."
[SISTEMA] "PENALTY: ACCESS SUSPENSION."
Out in the hall, someone knocks on your door. You hear it muffled, like sound underwater. No way you're answering. Not now.
Let me tell you something I learned late: when the deadline hits, people don't get smarter. They get more themselves.
{veia:1} You already got half a plan and three ways to game the clock. None of 'em work alone. Together, maybe.
{veia:2} Your body's ready. It's been ready for a day now. It's your head that needs to catch up.
{veia:3} You put together what you've seen the last two days, and the pattern's starting to show. Somebody's shoving rookies into the arena on purpose. You just don't know who's cashing in on it.
{veia:4} You already know who buys, who sells, and who owes. In a place like this, that's worth more than a punch.
{veia:5} The static's so loud you can barely hear the warning. And inside it, for the first time, a whole word: *come*.
One day. What you do with it says who you are.

choices.label: Head to the Arena and face whoever shows up
Find whoever's been looking for me
Grab the official mission from the terminal
Find somebody who knows more than you

title: The Nameless Fighter
text: She stops. And smiles under the hood.
[???] "Good. There's something there."
She cuts her own connection before the end. The ring's empty. The system doesn't even know what result to log.
On your display, a message: an address and a word.
*About time.*

title: Official Mission
text: That plaza terminal? Yeah, it was waiting for you.
[SISTEMA] "OFFICIAL MISSION: RANKED KILL."
[SISTEMA] "TAKE DOWN A RANKED OPPONENT IN THE EAST ARENA."
[SISTEMA] "REWARD: 500 CREDITS. FAILURE PENALTY: 7-DAY SUSPENSION."
Five hundred credits. More than you've ever had in here. Maybe more than you'll ever get.
You confirm. The terminal chirps, that obnoxiously cheerful sound only a machine makes when it's about to ruin your day.
East Arena's fifteen minutes out. The vendor from the market down below told you to stay away from the East Zone today.
*Coincidence.*
You don't believe that for a second.

title: Ranked Kill
text: The chat that was laughing at you is now screaming your name. Wrong, but they're saying it.
[SISTEMA] "RANKED KILL COMPLETE. SUSPENSION LIFTED. +500 CREDITS."
On the way out, in the shoving, someone in a hoodie bumps your shoulder and vanishes into the crowd.
There's a note in your inventory. An address and a word.
*Took long enough.*

title: Training
text: Nobody gets good at anything stuck in a cube. You head out to train.

{veia:1} You burn the whole afternoon in front of a busted service panel behind the low market. Pull a wire, it locks up. Pull another, it beeps. Thirtieth time you get it: the panel isn't a lock, it's a question. And every question has a loose end.

{veia:2} You pay five credits to get beat by a training robot in the Arena. It hits, you go down. Hits, you go down. Around the twentieth fall your body stops dropping like a sack and starts dropping like somebody who's gonna get up.

{veia:3} You sit in front of the plaza terminal and read, one by one, the logs of who came through in the last twenty-four hours. It's boring. It's real boring. And in the middle of the boring there's a timestamp that doesn't match anything.

{veia:4} You go back to the low market and stay. Buy a coffee you didn't need, a rumor you already knew, a conversation that wasn't going anywhere. End of the day you know what every mouth in that basement costs.

{veia:5} You lie on the cube floor, close your eyes, and stop fighting the static. Let it come. It comes. And for the first time you find where it lives: a frequency, narrow, like an old radio finding a station.
There's no music swelling, no crowd clapping. Training is this: repeating something ugly until it's yours.

title: Who Teaches
text: Some shit you can't train solo. You need someone who's already taken more hits than you.

{veia:1} In the back of the low market there's an old lady who fixes SBIs under the counter. She watches you poke at a terminal for three minutes and laughs. "You open the door and leave your footprint on the mat, kid." She shows you how to come and go without the system knowing you passed.

{veia:2} A retired fighter, four-digit rank back in the day, leaning on the ropes of the Training Arena. He doesn't teach you a single move. He just has you watch his shoulder. Three hours staring at a shoulder. By the end, you see the punch before he throws it.

{veia:3} A data dealer who lost everything in a betting scheme spots you a coffee and teaches you a lesson without realizing it. "Forget what the guy says. Watch where the money went." He's talking about himself. You take notes on all of it.

{veia:4} A felt hat vendor, the same one who gave you the free tip, pulls you aside. "You're learning fast. So learn this last one: everybody lies with their hands, not their mouth." He shows you. You'll never unsee it.
{veia:5} It's nobody. It's the static. It stops being noise and becomes a full voice, old, way older than the LDI. She doesn't teach you anything. She just waits for you to answer. And you answer.
The ones who truly teach never charge up front. You'll pay later, one way or another. You always pay.
